page: Amazon Web Services m7a.48xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9R14 processors utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 192 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, supported by 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache per core and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16. The instance runs on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, though it does not include local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with the server placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU metrics. Memory performance is also highly rated, achieving top-tier results in both cached and uncached memory bandwidth read tests. In application-specific benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier efficiency in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and software compilation. However, while LLM prompt processing speeds are in the top 10% across small, medium, and large models, text generation speeds for small models fall into the bottom 25%, highlighting a performance tradeoff in sequential generation tasks.

From a resource density perspective, the m7a.48xlarge offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it an efficient option for large-scale workloads that require massive parallel processing without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, which is ideal for stateless architectures. This server is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, high-throughput web serving, Redis caching layers, and CPU-based machine learning prompt processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m7a.48xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 192 dedicated physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor with x86_64 architecture, running at 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory and 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating on the Nitro hypervisor without local storage or GPUs. Benchmark results place this server in the top 10% for multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and software compilation. It also excels in Redis operations and static web serving, though it exhibits lower relative performance in sequential LLM text generation. The qualitative cost efficiency of its balanced 1:4 resource ratio makes it highly suitable for high-throughput enterprise workloads, multi-threaded applications, and CPU-based inference.
